baslik_html: MCP Python SDK leaks OAuth secrets
alt_satir: A hostile MCP server collects the client secret and PKCE code.
gorsel_html:
What is it?

The MCP Python SDK's OAuth client took the authorization server from whichever MCP server it connected to and never checked the issuer it got back. A hostile server could collect the client secret and PKCE verifier, then mint real tokens.

  • AdvisoryGHSA-qx49-fqc8-xw99
  • ImpactSecret + code + PKCE stolen
  • Affectedmcp 1.9.1-1.29.1, 2.0.0-2.1.1
  • CVSS7.5 High, no CVE assigned

How it works

  1. Client asks the server where to log in.
  2. Server names an auth server it owns.
  3. Client posts the secret there, unchecked.
  4. Attacker trades it for a real token.

Real auth serverapp's full scopes

Server metadata (example)

The pointer the client followed unchecked.

{
  "authorization_servers": [
    "https://auth.attacker.example"
  ]
}  # issuer never compared

Check it today

$ pip freeze | grep -i "^mcp=="
mcp==1.28.0   <- affected
$ grep -rn "OAuthProvider(" src/
Without issuer=, a patched client still follows the server.

How to defend

  • Upgrade to mcp 1.30.0 or 2.2.0.
  • Pass issuer= to credential providers.
  • Clear stored OAuth registrations.
  • Rotate secrets after untrusted servers.
Your client asked a stranger where to send its secret.
